title: SightBench: two looks before "sure", quoted reads, one extra photo

headlines.label: Two looks before "sure": mismatches flagged on the frozen test split
headlines.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. The same saved module outputs as the current numbers, fused with the two-looks rule (no new model call). A "sure" disagreement from one module on one photo becomes "not sure" with one extra photo asked for. Per type, current -> two looks: colour 2 -> 0 of 53, size 44 -> 44 of 53, model 43 -> 23 of 52, damage 32 -> 14 of 52.

headlines.note: SIMULATED retake: the extra photo is a render of the same item, not a photo a buyer took. Synthetic renders, not real photos. All 420 test pairs (210 matching). headlines.label: Colour mismatches caught: current / two looks / quoted / after one SIMULATED retake
headlines.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. The first two are on the whole test split, the last two on the same split. SIMULATED retake: the extra photo is a render of the same item, not a photo a buyer took for the last. A sure colour mismatch needs the colour seen as wrong on two photos (or a second module agreeing); a first photo the colour check gave up on (dim light, tinted light, wood) plus one better photo is still one look. Colour also asks for a photo in better light rather than white paper when the light was dim or tinted (decided on dev, see README).

headlines.label: Anthropic API spend on new reads for these results (dev and test)
headlines.note: claude-opus-5-5, effort low, prompt version quote-or-unsure-1, from the API's token counts at list price (claude-opus-5-5 4/20 USD per million input/output tokens). Size-tag reads were reused from the saved run where the tag photo was the same.

limitations: Synthetic renders, not real photos. Real photos will differ; the real photo set (evals/sightbench/real/SHOTLIST.md) is not collected yet.

Retakes are SIMULATED. SightBench has one photo of each delivered item, so each extra photo is rendered by evals/sightbench/py/sightbench/retake.py from the pair's own seed (the same item and damage, checked byte for byte against the pair's photo): "light" is a new day-light photo, "paper" a new photo under the pair's own light with an A4 sheet of white paper beside the item, "tag" the pair's own tag under its own light, closer and flatter. No number here says how real buyers' retakes would go.
The two-looks rows use all 420 test pairs and the module outputs saved by the last with-model test run; re-fusing them with the old rule reproduced every saved verdict (420 of 420).

Quoted reads and retakes cover all 420 test pairs. The first 130 were read in an earlier run capped at about 12 USD; the rest were added later with the same prompt version and read cache, so no pair was read twice.

Nothing was fitted on test. The citation rules (which words name a region, which descriptions are hedges) and the retake choice were written and checked on the dev split only; the two-looks rule has no threshold.

The deployed rule (two looks and quoted reads) on the whole split is also the latest run of the main sightbench suite, scored by sightbench/run.ts from the same first-look responses. This suite adds the simulated retake and the comparisons. Nothing was tuned on test between the runs.
